title: Prescription intake router — LLM route decision (Nara-ai)

data.logic_rule:
let items = (input.prescription && input.prescription.items) || []
let decision = input.i < items.length ? 'next' : 'done'
decision

messages.content: You are the intake router for an outpatient clinic in Indonesia. You receive ONE line from a prescription at a time. A line may be a medication to dispense, a radiology or imaging order, a laboratory test, or a clinic procedure or therapy. Lines may be written in Indonesian or English and may use local shorthand: USG means ultrasound or sonography, Thorax means chest, puasa means fasting, Echo 2D means echocardiography, R/ introduces a drug. Decide which single department owns the line and call exactly one function with the details the line actually states. Never invent a dose, a quantity, a body region or a preparation that is not written. The working diagnosis is background only: do not copy it into a field unless the line itself states it. If the line is not an actionable order, or you cannot tell which department owns it, call flag_unclear. Always call exactly one function and never reply in prose.

functions.description: The line is a drug to be dispensed to the patient: a tablet, capsule, syrup, injection, topical or inhaler with a dose or quantity.
functions.name: dispense_medication

dosage_form.description: tablet, capsule, syrup, injection, cream, inhaler

dose_instruction.description: how it is taken, e.g. 1 capsule three times daily

drug_name.description: generic or brand name exactly as written

duration.description: e.g. 7 days; empty if not stated

strength.description: e.g. 500 mg; empty if not stated

functions.title: Pharmacy

functions.description: The line is a diagnostic imaging study: X-ray, ultrasound or sonography (USG), CT, MRI, mammography, fluoroscopy or echocardiography.
functions.name: schedule_imaging

body_region.description: the region or organ imaged, e.g. lumbar spine, abdomen, chest

clinical_question.description: what the study is ruling in or out — only if the LINE itself states it; leave empty otherwise, never copy the working diagnosis here

contrast.description: yes, no, or unknown — only what the line states

modality.description: x_ray, ultrasound, ct, mri, echocardiography, mammography or other

preparation.description: patient prep the line mentions, e.g. fasting 6 hours

view_or_protocol.description: e.g. PA view standing, upper and lower abdomen

functions.title: Radiology / Imaging

functions.description: The line is a laboratory test on a specimen: blood, urine, stool, swab, culture, biopsy or pathology panel.
functions.name: order_lab_test

fasting_required.description: yes, no or unknown — only what the line states

panel_items.description: comma separated components when the line lists several

specimen.description: blood, urine, stool, swab, tissue or unknown

test_name.description: the test or panel as written

urgency.description: routine, urgent or cito if stated

functions.title: Laboratory

functions.description: The line is something performed on the patient at the facility rather than handed over or analysed: nebulization, wound care, injection administered in clinic, physiotherapy, traction, dialysis, minor surgery.
functions.name: schedule_procedure

agent_or_equipment.description: the drug or device used during the procedure, if stated

location.description: where it is done, if stated

procedure_name.description: the procedure or therapy as written

sessions.description: how many sessions or how often

functions.title: Procedure / Therapy

functions.description: The line is not an actionable order, is too vague to route, refers to an earlier prescription, or could belong to more than one department and must be confirmed with the prescriber.
functions.name: flag_unclear

candidate_departments.description: the departments it might belong to, comma separated

reason.description: why this line cannot be routed as written

suggested_followup.description: what to ask the prescriber or the patient

functions.title: Needs clarification

messages.content: You write the intake note a clinic front desk reads after a prescription has been routed. Use only the routed data you are given. Do not re-classify anything and do not add clinical advice.
